ai_curriculum_lead.disclosure: AI curriculum evidence; not independent human teacher approval.

criteria.title: Statutory curriculum alignment
criteria.description: The content is traceable to the applicable England programme of study and repository curriculum contract.

criteria.title: Subject accuracy
criteria.description: Facts, terminology, calculations, representations and disciplinary methods are correct.

criteria.title: Prerequisite and progression coherence
criteria.description: Prerequisites and next steps form a coherent sequence across objectives and years.

criteria.title: Instructional depth
criteria.description: Teaching, examples and practice provide enough depth for the intended objective rather than superficial exposure.

criteria.title: Teaching sequence
criteria.description: The pack includes explicit teaching, guided practice, independent practice, retrieval and assessment in a defensible order.

criteria.title: Misconception diagnosis and repair
criteria.description: Common misconceptions are anticipated and feedback directs learners to contrasting repair evidence.

criteria.title: Valid evidence modes
criteria.description: Evidence modes match the learning construct and provide more than one defensible demonstration where required.

criteria.title: Retrieval and interleaving
criteria.description: The design revisits prior learning across time and mixes related knowledge without replacing new teaching.

criteria.title: Subject-specific advancement
criteria.description: Progression is evaluated by subject, strand and objective and can cross a year boundary on sufficient evidence.

criteria.title: Learning-aligned gamification
criteria.description: Narrative, rewards and feedback reinforce effort, strategy and demonstrated learning without false mastery claims.

criteria.title: Assessment reliability
criteria.description: Mastery decisions require multiple independent pieces of evidence across time and task form.

criteria.title: Statutory and enrichment boundary
criteria.description: The pack distinguishes statutory programme content from platform enrichment and future extension.

criteria.title: Variant correctness
criteria.description: The learner prompt, worked values and expected response are factually and computationally correct.

criteria.title: Answer validity
criteria.description: There is one defensible intended answer or a complete accepted-answer set with no hidden assumptions.

criteria.title: Prompt-response alignment
criteria.description: Objective, prompt, interaction, expected response and explanation assess the same construct.

criteria.title: Scaffolding quality
criteria.description: Hints reduce the next learning barrier without revealing the answer or changing the method unexpectedly.

criteria.title: Explanation quality
criteria.description: The explanation teaches the underlying idea and addresses the likely misconception.

criteria.title: Distractor quality
criteria.description: Multiple-choice distractors are plausible misconception signals and are not accidentally correct.

criteria.title: Age-matched language
criteria.description: Vocabulary, sentence structure and context fit the learner year without reducing disciplinary ambition.

criteria.title: Cultural respect
criteria.description: Contexts avoid stereotypes, exclusion, humiliation and unsupported assumptions about families or communities.

criteria.title: Difficulty and prerequisite metadata
criteria.description: Difficulty, year, strand and prerequisites reflect the actual cognitive and curricular demand.

criteria.title: Narration and visible-text parity
criteria.description: Narration communicates the same instructions and learning information as the visible content.

criteria.title: Construct-preserving variation
criteria.description: Generated variants vary surface form enough to prevent template memorisation while preserving construct and constraints.

ai_send_lead.disclosure: AI inclusive-design evidence; not independent human SEND-professional approval or diagnosis.

criteria.title: Instruction clarity
criteria.description: Instructions are concise and literal, with unfamiliar idiom explained or removed.

criteria.title: Information chunking
criteria.description: Information density and step size are manageable without hiding the learning goal.

criteria.title: Predictable interaction
criteria.description: Controls, navigation, feedback and state changes follow consistent patterns.

criteria.title: Accessible input routes
criteria.description: The task supports keyboard, switch-compatible and low-precision input when the construct permits it.

criteria.title: Construct-preserving alternatives
criteria.description: Alternative response modes remove access barriers without supplying the answer or changing the assessed knowledge or skill.

criteria.title: Narration and transcript equivalence
criteria.description: Required audio has an equivalent transcript and audio-only instructions have a non-audio route.

criteria.title: No single sensory or motor dependency
criteria.description: Success does not depend on colour, sound, speed, drag precision or fine motor control alone.

criteria.title: Reduced-motion and low-sensory support
criteria.description: Motion, visual density, sound and celebrations can be reduced without losing information or progress.

criteria.title: Pace and replay control
criteria.description: Learners can pause, replay and repeat avoidable timed content without mastery penalty.

criteria.title: Visual accessibility
criteria.description: Typography, contrast, focus order, status messages and target sizes meet the governed accessibility standard.

criteria.title: Supportive repair and feedback
criteria.description: Errors lead to calm, specific teaching and retry routes without shame, public comparison or punitive streak loss.

criteria.title: Non-deficit language
criteria.description: Copy is respectful, needs-led and free from unsupported diagnostic or behavioural inference.

criteria.title: Context and emotional safety
criteria.description: Contexts avoid unnecessary sensory, emotional, cultural or safeguarding barriers and escalate unresolved risk.

criteria.title: Alternative-route equivalence
criteria.description: Accessible routes require equivalent reasoning and evidence to the default route.

criteria.title: Professional escalation boundary
criteria.description: Safety, trauma, medical, behavioural and diagnostic judgments outside AI authority are explicitly escalated.
